text:
marina: quick question about a helm edge case — trying to let chart consumers override a secret name but fall back to a global secret. if they set `values.app.env.extraSecretName: null` i want it to use `values.app.env.secretName` instead. current template behaves oddly when extraSecretName is explicitly null or empty string. any ideas?

sam: are these secrets created by external-secrets or by the chart itself? that changes whether we should hard-fail.

marina: external-secrets is used in several clusters, but in some envs the secret is created later. so we should avoid helm install failing if secret missing.

devon: ok. two separate concerns: 1) choosing the name (override vs fallback) and 2) keeping install idempotent when secret doesn't exist yet. for (1) helm's `default` is usually fine — it treats empty string and nil as empty, so `| default` will pick the fallback. example: 

```yaml
{{- $secret := .Values.app.env.extraSecretName | default .Values.app.env.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ $secret | quote }}
      optional: {{ default true .Values.app.env.secretOptional }}
```

That handles null/empty. for (2) set `optional: true` on the secretRef so k8s doesn't error if secret absent. we default optional to true for external-secrets workflows.

alex: small note: `default` will also replace `0` or `false` if those are passed — but not relevant here. if you want to be explicit about null vs empty you could do an `if` with `ne` or `len`. e.g. `if (and (not (empty .Values.app.env.extraSecretName)) )` then use it else fallback.

sam: do we need `lookup` to test for an existing k8s secret and conditionally render the envFrom only if it exists? i've used that to avoid mounting a secret env when it's completely absent and optional isn't desired.

devon: you can, but `lookup` causes Helm to query the cluster at render time which is fine for installs against cluster but makes `helm template` not reflect runtime. simpler is optional:true — k8s will ignore missing secret. if you really need to avoid creating the envFrom chunk in the manifest, `lookup` snippet: 

```yaml
{{- $ns := .Release.Namespace }}
{{- $exists := (lookup "v1" "Secret" $ns (default "" $secret)) }}
{{- if $exists }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ $secret | quote }}
{{- end }}
```

Note: `lookup` returns an object; you often check `len` on `.items` or non-nil `.metadata` depending on API. that makes templates cluster-aware.

marina: nice, thanks. one more subtlety — consumers of the chart might pass `extraSecretName: ""` (empty string) in their values file. `default` will consider that empty and use fallback, right?

devon: yes. `default` treats empty string as empty and will return the second arg. so you're covered. just ensure your values doc states the precedence: `extraSecretName` > `secretName` and `secretOptional` defaults true.

alex: i'd add a short example in `values.schema.json` and the chart README so folks don't accidentally pass `null` and expect helm to error. also ping codeowners for a tiny PR to update docs.

marina: will do. i'll push a small patch that implements the `default` + `optional` approach and update README/values.schema. tagging @devon for a quick review when i open the PR. thanks all :tada:

infra-bot: CI lint: helm lint passed on branch/feature/helm-secret-fallback (no blocking issues).

devon: ack, i'll review once the PR hits.

marina: thanks — closing this thread once PR is out.
